title: Why can't we just print more money? 💸
description:
Ten apples, ten dollars, and a money printer: the simplest way to understand inflation, and what happened when Zimbabwe tried it.

Sources: Hanke & Kwok, Cato Journal (2009); Reserve Bank of Zimbabwe Z$100 trillion note, Jan 2009.

humour.trend: 'you the birthday' (TikTok slang this week: you're great)

meta.overrides: first video with Blender 3D shots (cinematic style test)

speaker: ved

scenes.say: Why can't a country just *print more money*, and make everyone rich?
Picture a tiny country with *ten apples* and *ten dollars*. One apple costs one dollar.

scenes.say: So sellers raise the price. Each apple now costs *two dollars*. That's *inflation*.

beat.text:
The printer: "I'm the birthday."
Prices: *"Me too."*

scenes.say: Zimbabwe tried it. In 2008, prices *doubled* about every day, and it printed a *one hundred trillion* dollar note.

scenes.say: Money isn't wealth. It's a ticket for the stuff we make. Print more tickets, and each one *buys less*.
